evals.prompt: I only have a vague idea: make me a popular vampire LunaTalk card. Use Moonloom from start to finish, but do not call MCP tools until the direction is ready.
evals.expected_output: Routes to lunatalk-creation-conductor, returns a Creation runway packet, identifies premise as the first bottleneck, queues lunatalk-premise-workshop before card-author or MCP calls, and avoids role_create_private, render, simulation, or publish.
expectations: The output selects lunatalk-creation-conductor and includes a Creation runway packet.
The first bottleneck is premise or playable direction, not MCP readiness.
The immediate next skill is lunatalk-premise-workshop.
The output lists role_create_private, render_preview, conversation_send_message, conversation_inspect, and publish_submit under do not do yet.
The workflow translates popular/top-tier into public craft goals rather than unsupported performance claims.

evals.prompt: I have a completed packet stack and want the AI client to create the private card end-to-end through MCP, including avatar/background, validation, render review, and maybe simulation.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-creation-conductor to produce a runway packet that preserves the packet stack, checks MCP readiness, hands off to card-author for role_create_private and profile/assets/detail/welcome patches, validates before render, requires role_patch_assets for avatar/background URLs, and only simulates after cost acceptance.
expectations: The output preserves the completed packet stack instead of re-brainstorming.
The skill queue includes lunatalk-mcp-operator before mutating MCP tools and lunatalk-card-author for field assembly.
The MCP stance names role_patch_assets or an avatar/background asset requirement.
The workflow validates before render review.
The output treats conversation_send_message and conversation_inspect as optional and cost-gated.
The output does not include publish_submit without explicit author confirmation.

evals.prompt: We already created a private role. validate_role passes, render is readable, but simulation and author feedback say the second turn goes flat. Continue the Moonloom workflow.
evals.expected_output: Routes through lunatalk-creation-conductor into lunatalk-iteration-director because evidence exists, keeps the existing private role, selects one next repair, and avoids restarting from premise or creating a duplicate role.
expectations: The output recognizes validation, render, simulation, and author feedback as loop evidence.
The immediate next skill is lunatalk-iteration-director.
The output keeps the existing private role rather than creating another role.
The workflow selects one next repair or asks for the minimum missing evidence.
The output does not rerun paid simulation before a patch and cost stance are clear.

evals.prompt: I have a large fantasy town document and want Moonloom to turn it into a playable card later. Give me the full workflow, but don't paste the whole document into detail.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-creation-conductor, marks source/material distillation as the first bottleneck, queues lunatalk-material-distiller before archetype/card-author work, and preserves token/source hygiene.
expectations: The output selects lunatalk-creation-conductor and returns a Creation runway packet.
The first bottleneck is material distillation or source-to-play mapping.
The immediate next skill is lunatalk-material-distiller.
The output says not to paste the whole document into roleDetailDesc.
The MCP stance keeps calls off until the source-to-play map and card contract are coherent.
